rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed position permits eating meat slaughtered without invoking God’s name whether the omission was deliberate or forgetful; Ibn Abi Layla and al-Awza‘i also transmit it.
rows.anchor: metrûkü’t-tesmiye olanın ekli helâl olduğuna kāil olmuştur ki bu kavil, İbn Ebî Leylâ ve Evzâî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired commands and prohibitions in the slaughter and hunting verses clearly make invoking God’s name obligatory; their explicit wording cannot be neglected when reconciliation is possible.
rows.anchor: nehyiyle mâkablindeki فَكُلُوا۟ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ emrinin tekābül-i tâmmından zebh ve saydda tesmiyenin farziyeti pek zâhir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa rules that meat is not eaten when a Muslim deliberately omits the invocation, but is eaten when it was forgotten.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretleri de “eğer müslim tesmiyeyi amden terk ederse yenmez, unutur da terk ederse yenir” demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Maliki school’s most preferred transmitted position is also Abu Hanifa’s distinction between deliberate omission and forgetfulness; Ibn Atiyya calls it the majority view.
rows.anchor: İmam Mâlik’ten de Mâlikiyyece en muhtâr rivayet budur. İbn Atıyye bunun cumhur kavli olduğunu söylemiştir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali, İbn Abbas, Mücâhid, Atâ b. Ebî Rebah, Saîd b. Müseyyeb, İbn Şihâb ve Tâvûs
rows.claim: They hold that there is no problem in eating an animal slaughtered when the invocation was forgotten.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den, İbn Abbas’tan, Mücâhid’den, Atâ b. Ebî Rebah’tan, Saîd b. Müseyyeb’den, İbn Şihâb ve Tâvûs’tan mervîdir ki bu zevât “üzerine tesmiye unutulup da zebh olunanın eklinde beis yoktur”

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: Ali says the invocation question is grounded in religious affiliation, implying the distinction concerns deliberate repudiation.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali إ ََّنما هِيَ عَلَى الْمِل َّةِ yani tesmiye meselesi ancak din üzerine mübtenîdir demiş

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that remembrance of God by a Muslim is present in the heart.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas da “müslimin zikrullah kalbindedir”

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says invoking God’s name gives no benefit in polytheism, while forgetfulness causes no harm within the faith community.
rows.anchor: “şirkte ismin menfaati olmadığı gibi, millette de nisyânın zararı yoktur”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse addresses deliberate omission, since it is agreed that someone who forgets is not called impious; impiety applies to deliberate conduct.
rows.anchor: unutana “fâsık” denilmeyeceği müttefekun aleyhtir. Fısk ancak amde nisbet olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failing to invoke God’s name over slaughter or game, and eating what lacks that invocation, are each acts of fisq, disobedience to the command.
rows.anchor: Yani zebh u sayd üzerine Allah’ın ismi zikredilmemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s rationale of fisq reinforces the prohibition on both omission of the invocation and eating such meat, and indicates deliberate action.
rows.anchor: أَلَّا تَأْكُلُوا۟ nehyi böyle fısk ile ta‘lîl olunarak tekid buyurulmuştur ki bu hem terk-i tesmiyeden nehyi hem de ekilden nehyi tazammun ve amdi iktizâ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking God’s name is an obligatory condition of valid slaughter, but forgetfully omitting it does not invalidate the slaughter, just as forgetful eating does not invalidate a fast.
rows.anchor: nisyan ile terk-i tesmiye de tezkiyeyi müfsid olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasmiya means mentioning God’s name in any manner and is broader than the specific basmala formula.
rows.anchor: tesmiye, ismullâhı herhangi bir suretle zikretmektir ve “besmele”den e‘amdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasmiya may consist of phrases such as Allahu akbar, subhanallah, or la ilaha illa Allah, and may be spoken in a language other than Arabic.
rows.anchor: “Allahu ekber” veya “sübhânallah” veya “lâ ilâhe illallah” demek de bir tesmiye, bir zikirdir. Arapça’dan mâ‘adâ lisan ile de olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basmala is the particular formula ‘In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate,’ or simply ‘In the name of God.’
rows.anchor: Besmele ise بَسِْمِ اللهِّٰ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّح۪يمِ veya sadece بَسِْمِ اللهِّٰ demektir ve bir tesmiye-i mahsûsadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verses command invocation of God’s name generally, the obligation is tasmiya rather than basmala; basmala is nevertheless sunnah.
rows.anchor: Âyetlerde emrolunan da ale’l-ıtlâk ismullâhın zikri olduğundan farz, besmele değil tesmiyedir. Velâkin bu tesmiyenin besmele ile olması da sünnettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For slaughter, the sunnah invocation is ‘In the name of God’; adding ‘God is greatest’ is better, while the sunnah invocation when eating is the full basmala.
rows.anchor: zebihde tesmiyenin sünneti sadece بِاسْمِ اللهِّٰ demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion directs readers to the prohibitions on carrion, the exception for properly slaughtered animals, and the permissibility of wholesome food and the People of the Book’s food.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Mâide’ye حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ [5/3] sahifesine اِلاَّ مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ [5/3] ve اَلْيَوْمَ اُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُۜ وَطَعَامُ الَّذ۪ينَ اُو۫تُوا الْكِتَابَ حِلٌّ لَكُمْ [5/5] bak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when no outward harm is apparent, food lacking God’s name is certainly fisq and carries inward spiritual harm and punishment.
rows.anchor: bunun zâhiren başka fenalığını ve açık bir zararını anlamasanız bile her hâlde bir fısk olduğunu ve zarar-ı bâtınî ve mânevîsi ve bir cezâsı bulunduğunu muhakkak biliniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The satans are Iblis and his jinn forces, while their allies are human satans and their followers.
rows.anchor: “Şeyâtîn”den murad gizli şeytanlar İblis ve cünûdu, yani şeyâtîn-i cin, bunların dostlarından murad da şeyâtîn-i ins ve etbâ‘ı olduğu zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from Ikrima identifies the satans as rebellious Magians and their allies as the Quraysh polytheists.
rows.anchor: İkrime’den bir rivayette denilmiştir ki “şeyâtîn”den murad Mecûs mütemerridleri, dostlarından murad da Kureyş müşrikleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Magians and Quraysh had bonds of friendship and correspondence; after carrion was forbidden, Persian Magians wrote to Quraysh mocking the Muslims’ distinction between their own slaughter and animals that died naturally.
rows.anchor: câhiliyede dostluk ve mükâtebe cereyan ederdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The satanic prompting seeks to make people eat carrion and visible or hidden impurities and act against God’s command.
rows.anchor: İşte şeytanlar insanlara böyle telkīnât ile lâşeleri, görünür görünmez pislikleri yedirmeye ve Allah’ın emri hilâfına sevk etmeye çalışırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying those who urge this conduct makes people polytheists; failing to invoke God’s name over hunted or slaughtered food, or eating it without invocation, goes beyond fisq and amounts to or leads to shirk.
rows.anchor: Bunun için zebh veya sayd olunup yenecek şeyler üzerine Allah’ın ismini zikretmemek veya üzerine Allah’ın ismi zikredilmeyen şeylerden yemek sade bir fısk olarak kalmaz. Şirk veya şirke müeddî de olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the upright religion and the way of Abraham, who turned wholly toward God alone and was not among the polytheists.
rows.anchor: yani hâli hanîf, bir Allah’a müteveccih olan İbrâhim milletine hidâyet etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan polytheists, Jews, and Christians who claim affiliation with Abraham are not his model, since they divide religion.
rows.anchor: Onun milletine intisab iddia eden ehl-i Mekke ve Yehûd ve Nasârâ gibi dini tefrik edenlerden değil idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyaman is a verbal noun used adjectivally in an intensive sense, meaning upright; a reported reading with an opened kaf and doubled, kasra yā means very straight and firm.
rows.anchor: “Kıyemen”, “kıyam” mânasına ve mübalağa suretiyle vasf bi’lmasdardır. Kâf’ın fethi ve yâ’nın teşdid ve kesriyle مُسْتَقِيمٍۢ kıraatleri de vardır ki pek doğru ve sâbit demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dīn qayyim is expressed in practice by declaring that prayer, worship or sacrifices, life, and death belong wholly to God, who has no partner.
rows.anchor: Hepsi Allah içindir. {لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُۥ} O’nun hiç şerîki yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every act and worship must be performed with this belief, intention, and sincerity of exclusive devotion.
rows.anchor: Yani her ibadet, her iş bu akide, bu niyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is first among those who submit to God, meaning foremost in surrendering to God’s command.
rows.anchor: Ben ise Müslimînin evveliyim, yani Allah’ın emrine teslim olanların birincisiyim, en önündeyim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This states the Prophet’s prompt obedience and shows that the divine commands apply to everyone, so all Muslims must follow him.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber’in me’mur olduğu evâmir-i ilâhiyeye sür‘at-i imtisâlini ve o evâmirin kendine mahsus olmayıp umûmun bunlarla me’mur olduğunu ve bütün Müslüman olanların ona iktidâsı lüzûmunu beyandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers urged Muhammad to return to their religion, promising to provide whatever he wanted in this world and the next, and told believers to follow them with the promise of bearing their sins.
rows.anchor: “yâ Muhammed, gel bizim dinimize dön, dünya ve âhiret ne istersen biz tekeffül ederiz”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God is Lord of everything, the Prophet will seek no other lord.
rows.anchor: Rabbi iken ben ondan başka bir rab mı isteyeceğim?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul bears responsibility for its own deeds; neither committing sin nor bearing its punishment can be delegated to another.
rows.anchor: ne günah yapmakta ne de cezâsını çekmekte vekâlet, niyâbet cereyan etmez. Herkes yaptığı günahı kendi yapar ve cezâsını kendi çeker

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who promises to bear another’s sin lies; the sinner bears the consequence of the act, while the deceiver also bears punishment for lying, urging sin, and making the false promise.
rows.anchor: Günahı yapan yaptığının cezâsını çeker, öyle deyip yalan söyleyen, günaha teşvik eden de bu yalanının, bu teşvik ve iğfâlinin, bu fena taahhüdünün cezâsını çeker

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Individual responsibility does not mean a deed harms only its actor; each deed also concerns those involved in proportion to their connection with it.
rows.anchor: Ancak her fiil fâiline nisbet olunur ve her günahın alâkadar olanlara alâkaları nisbetinde ta‘alluku bulunur demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people ultimately return to God, who will disclose the truth about the matters over which they differed.
rows.anchor: nihâyet hepinizin merci‘i Rabbinizdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because everyone will face final accountability, people should consider God’s judgment and act with sincere intention instead of following competing religions, schools, or desires.
rows.anchor: samimi bir niyet ve ihlâs ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity, especially Muhammad’s community, succeeds earlier nations and is appointed to possess, govern, and carry out God’s rulings on earth, bearing responsibility for that trust.
rows.anchor: siz ümmet-i Muhammed, hepsinin halefi olmuş, yerlerine ikāme edilmiş bulunuyorsunuz. Allah’ın bundan böyle yeryüzünde temellük ve tasarruf ve icrâ-yı ahkâm edecek olan me’murları, mes’ulleri sizsiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised some people above others in degrees of intellect, knowledge, honor, status, wealth, and provision.
rows.anchor: Bir kısmınızı akl ü ilim, şeref ü câh, mâl ü rızık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different endowments test whether people use what they receive well and show gratitude; the best in deeds are chosen for future reward according to their works.
rows.anchor: verileni mahallinde hüsn-i isti‘mâl ile şükredip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is a realm of testing and competition: today’s condition results from yesterday’s test, and tomorrow’s will result from today’s.
rows.anchor: Bu âlem böyle bir âlem-i imtihan ve müsâbakadır ve bugünkü vaziyet dünkü imtihânın bir neticesidir. Yarınki vaziyet de bu imtihanın bir neticesi olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad’s community is tested both among its own members and collectively against earlier communities, from whom it must learn to win the competition.
rows.anchor: ümmet-i Muhammed, yalnız kendi efrâd ve sunûfu beyninde değil, hey’et-i mecmû‘asıyla halef olduğu ümem-i sâlife ile de bir imtihâna tâbi‘dir ve onlardan ibret alıp müsâbakayı kazanmak ihtiyâcındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences in rank are necessary to this test: those high may fall and those low may rise, while higher rank brings greater danger and responsibility, so status should prompt effort rather than pride.
rows.anchor: tefâvüt-i merâtib bu imtihan ve müsâbakanın levâzımındandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s punishment is swift for those who fail to fulfill the duty and gratitude owed for His gifts, however high their position; what is coming is near.
rows.anchor: Verdiği sermâye-i ni‘metin hakkını edâ ve şükrünü îfâ etmeyen ehl-i küfr ü isyâna ne kadar yüksek mevki‘de olurlarsa olsunlar Rabbin murad ettiği zaman bir anda belâlarını verir. Zaten her gelecek olan yakındır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives and covers the faults of those who strive in their duty and gratitude and ultimately grants them varied mercy and happiness.
rows.anchor: Vazifesine cehd eden, imtihanda muvaffak olmaya çalışan ehl-i şükr ü tâatin kusurlarını mağfiret, ayıplarını setr ve sonunda kendilerini envâ‘-ı rahmet ü sa‘âdetle bekâm eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the surah’s Meccan revelation and later Islamic history, this verse’s predictions about the future have clearly manifested and continue to do so, opening a new human history through Muhammad’s mission that surpasses prior peoples.
rows.anchor: bu sûrenin Mekke’de nâzil olduğu zamanı, bir de ondan sonra târîh-i İslâm’ın safahâtı düşünülürse, bu âyetin istikbâle müte‘allik ne kadar mucizeleri ihtivâ ettiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The succession and testing announced here continue from the past and are developed in the following surah, al-A‘raf.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin tazammun ettiği istihlâf ve imtihânın mâzîden beri sûret-i cereyânını tasvir ve tafsil edecek olan Sûre-i A‘râf’ı dinleyelim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created humanity before any human individual existed, determining and bringing its first substance into being before people took their present form.
rows.anchor: Siz hiçbir şey değil iken, siz nev‘-i beşerden hiçbir ferd âlemde mevcut değil iken, siz henüz şu bulunduğunuz şekl ü sureti ahz etmeden evvel ilk mayanızı takdir ve îcad eyledik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then shaped people from initially formless matter, clay on earth, and a seed in their fathers’ loins into the perfected human form.
rows.anchor: Siz ibtidâ-i hilkatte suretsiz, uzviyetsiz bir mahluk, arzda bir çamur ve babanızın sulbünde birer zerre, birer nutfe olduğunuz hâlde sizi ahsen-i takvîm olan insan suretine koyduk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command for the angels to prostrate to Adam means that they should serve him with submission, obedience, and compliance.
rows.anchor: Ona boyun eğip itaat ve inkıyâd ile hizmet eyleyin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address to humanity concerns the human race as a whole, and the prostration of the angels to Adam is recalled as a favor to humankind.
rows.anchor: Bu hitapların bir ferde veya sınıfa değil, ale’l-umûm cins-i beşere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate honors the whole human species, including Adam’s descendants, rather than Adam alone.
rows.anchor: bu secde emri Hazret-i Âdem’in şahsına mahsus değil, zürriyeti de dâhil olmak üzere nev‘ine ait bir şeref ve imtiyazdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s descendants include eminent prophets of great resolve who are superior to Adam himself, supporting the species-wide meaning of the honor.
rows.anchor: Zürriyet-i Âdem içinde bizzat Hazret-i Âdem’den efdal olan ulü’l-azm enbiyâ-yı izâm gibi zevât bulunduğu şüphesiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse is better read by treating Adam as a universal exemplar representing human nature and the whole human species, not merely as the first individual.
rows.anchor: ale’l-umûm nev‘-i beşerin mâhiyetini temsil eden bir misâl-i kül

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As father of humanity, Adam potentially possessed the virtues and faculties that would appear in all his descendants; thus his creation, shaping, and the angels’ prostration encompass all humanity.
rows.anchor: bütün zürriyetinde tecellî edecek olan fezâil ü melekâtı da bilkuvve hâiz olmak itibariyle ebü’l-beşer olarak teemmül edildiği zamandır ki hilkat-i Âdem hilkat-i benî Âdem’i, tasvîr-i Âdem tasvîr-i benî Âdem’i, Âdem’e secde bütün nev‘-i beşere secdeyi mutazammın olduğu tevazzuh eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage clarifies the meaning of humanity’s appointment as successors on earth in al-An‘am.
rows.anchor: mânasını da tavzih eden bu âyetin mazmûnu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God bestowed such honor on humanity that He commanded angels to prostrate to Adam, and worshipping other than God after these gifts is profound abasement, ingratitude, and a cause of grave responsibility.
rows.anchor: Âdem’in melâikeye değil, melâikenin Âdem’e secde etmesini emretmiştir
